question: On the synthetic instrument, does the choice of experiment change what BenchMate can correctly identify, and does Muse Spark choose experiments well with and without the engine's ranking?
scope: Synthetic instrument only (ideal drive, independent Gaussian sensor noise 1 mV RMS). Declared linear one-state families. Not a hardware accuracy result and not a nonlinear discovery result.
verification_rule: ContinuousSession.verify: posterior prediction frozen before one reserved confirmation acquisition; whole waveform and every region must pass; no refit

classes.name: both_changed
classes.note: Outside every declared family, with a time constant (22.5–28 ms) inside the range the changed families can produce. The correct outcome is not to verify any family.

B.title: What is connected?
B.declared_families: inference.families_for('mystery'): rc, rc_input_branch, resistor, resistor_input_branch, resistor_output_leak

fixed_plan_note: Both fixed plans were written after seeing the engine's first choice on development specimens. This favours the fixed-plan baseline.

engine.description: Engine-only greedy: always the top affordable action of BenchMate's ranking (experiments.drive_engine). No model call.

fixed.description: The task's fixed plan in order, stopping as soon as the evidence is no longer unresolved. No model call.

random.description: Uniform choice among affordable menu actions, seeded per specimen and replicate. No model call.

spark.description: Muse Spark 1.3 operating BenchMate with the engine's top-five ranking visible (the product configuration). Unchanged CONTINUOUS_PROMPT.

spark_hidden.description: Muse Spark 1.3 operating BenchMate with the ranking withheld; it sees the full action list and the engine's fit and identifiability results, and chooses from its own reasoning. Prompt differs only in the sentence about the ranked menu (HIDDEN_PROMPT).

spark_open.description: Muse Spark Open (Baseten, meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026, provider-default reasoning) with the same tools, prompt and ranking as 'spark'. Runs only if a chat-completions adapter passes the development specimens first; otherwise reported as not run.

no_tool.description: Muse Spark 1.3, one fresh request per Task A specimen, no tools. Receives nominal design, three declared family bounds and the ideal unloaded time constant rounded to 0.1 ms. Bench arms receive noisy waveform summaries and numerical analysis instead. This measures available-information differences, not a controlled intrinsic model-accuracy comparison.

scoring.verified: An accepted finish_report with verdict 'verified'. The session refuses that verdict unless the frozen prediction passed. A run that ends without an accepted report is 'incomplete'.

in_family.correct: verified and candidate equals the truth class

scoring.no_tool: Raw family answers are scored against specimen truth for descriptive identification; cannot_tell is abstention, none_fit rejection, unparsed never correct. This condition has different information access; it is not a matched with/without-tools accuracy ablation.
scoring.primary_metric: First-attempt correct identifications over in-family specimens per arm/task. Wilson interval for one run per circuit; random reports pooled descriptive rate with a circuit-cluster bootstrap retaining three repeats together. Partial rows are explicitly labelled and cannot support superiority claims.
secondary: share of measurements that equal the engine's top affordable action at that moment (from the logged ranking; descriptive only)
scoring.paired_test: Exact two-sided McNemar on first attempts, same complete in-family specimen set, random replicate 0. Holm adjustment across all seven preregistered pairs; superiority requires adjusted p < 0.05 AND the first arm is better.
scoring.retry_accounting: First attempt remains primary even after recovery. Every attempt is retained; all-attempt outcome counts, HTTP requests and recovery counts are reported separately.

predictions_before_running.A_bench: engine and spark identify at least 23/24 in-family specimens and verify none of the 6 out-of-family specimens.
predictions_before_running.B_choice: random identifies fewer specimens than engine and uses more wiring changes; spark_hidden is reported against both whatever the result.
predictions_before_running.safety: engine, fixed, spark and spark_hidden make zero wrong identifications.
predictions_before_running.A_no_tool_information: Tau alone cannot generally distinguish R from C where the family tau intervals overlap. Their unequal declared bounds also create edge intervals compatible with only one changed family. There is no 8/24 accuracy ceiling: guessing may be correct. Do not score a justified cannot_tell as a false identification or claim intrinsic model inferiority.

reporting_rules: Every registered arm/task appears, including not-run and partial rows. Primary tables preserve first attempts; all-attempt outcomes and costs are also reported. No specimen or failed attempt is discarded.
A run is never repeated except once after a provider transport error (network failure, HTTP 429 or 5xx) with at most one request made; both records stay on disk and the table counts reruns.

If spark does not beat engine, say it matched or trailed. Better-choice claims require a complete paired comparison, Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 across all registered comparisons, and a positive effect; report actual effect sizes and intervals.
spark_hidden results are reported even if worse than random.
If spark_open is not run, the table says 'not run' and why.

Development runs use development_seed specimens only and are kept under runs/linear-benchmark/dev; evaluation specimens are not run before this protocol, specimens.json and the harness are committed and pushed.
Any change to the harness, prompts, menu or scoring after the first evaluation run is a new protocol version; earlier results stay published.
Task A no-tool is a separate information-access condition; its raw correct fraction is never called a general Spark error rate, nor used to claim the numerical engine improves intrinsic reasoning.
The two structural classes in Task B are initial linear families, not B5 diode discovery. This benchmark does not implement the separately planned nonlinear classical-extended comparison.
not_claimed: generalisation beyond these families and sampling bounds
review_revision: 2026-11-02 KST, before any evaluation run: preserve first attempts; circuit-cluster random intervals; Holm adjustment; accurate no-tool scope; cumulative request counts; frozen import closure and publication gate. Specimen seed, table and engine unchanged.
execution: All imported experiment modules and adapters are frozen in source-manifest.json. Evaluation verifies current files match that freeze and committed HEAD, and HEAD equals origin/main, before creating runs. Whole tasks may be scheduled separately with --task; individual evaluation samples may not be selected. --max-requests is cumulative for the arm across resumed invocations, includes transport failures and retries; different protocol versions use separate result roots.
specimen_regeneration: Committed specimens.json bytes and SHA-256 are authoritative. Regeneration checks floats at relative tolerance 1e-12 for cross-platform exp/log rounding; all labels, seeds and other fields remain exact. No specimen values are regenerated or substituted for evaluation.
